subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
Mentoring programme, session notes. Written by Vasudha, mentor.
Pooja (25), four months into the strategy team. Asked how meetings were going, she said, 'Fine. I mostly listen.'
When I pushed a little, it came out in a rush. 'Everyone in that room talks like they already know the answer. Rohit quotes numbers from memory. Sheetal just says, "Obviously we should…" and people nod. Inside I'm checking my point five times, and by the time I'm sure, the meeting has moved on.'
She said she'd had an idea about the pricing slide on Tuesday, and someone else said something similar ten minutes later, and it went into the plan. 'So maybe it wasn't special. Maybe I'm just not adding much.'
She laughed when she said it, but she didn't look up.
Next session: we'll talk about how everyone's outside looks, compared with her own inside. And one small point to say aloud next week.

qa.q: What did Pooja have an idea about on Tuesday?
qa.a: She had an idea about the pricing slide.

qa.q: What does Pooja believe about her place in the team, and what shows it?
qa.a: She feels discouraged and unsure she adds much, which shows when she says, 'Maybe I'm just not adding much,' without looking up.

qa.q: What small step could Pooja try to break the pattern of silence?
qa.a: She could say one point aloud early in a meeting, even before she is fully sure, so her ideas are heard and credited.

qa.q: How might Rohit and Sheetal look from their side of the table, compared with how Pooja sees them?
qa.a: They may have their own doubts too; Pooja only sees their confident outside, not whatever uncertainty they feel inside.

grounding: It shows a new hire comparing her inner doubts with colleagues' outer confidence, staying silent, and then taking her invisibility as proof she adds little.

subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
Wed, 11 pm
Same thing again today. Client call at four, eight of us on the screen. Nikita presented the market sizing like she was born doing it. Not one 'um'. The partner kept nodding.
I had a point about the rural distribution costs. I'd even checked it twice. I kept my mic on mute, waiting for the right moment, rehearsing the sentence. The moment didn't come. Or it came and I let it go.
At the end the partner said, 'Good session, team.' Nobody mentioned me because there was nothing to mention.
It's week nine. I think they've already filed me as the quiet one. Maybe that's accurate. Maybe the others just think faster.
Everyone else looks so sure. I'm sure they don't lie awake like this.
Tomorrow: internal review. I'll probably stay quiet there too.
— Gautam

qa.q: How many people were on the screen for the client call?
qa.a: Eight of us were on the screen for the client call.

qa.q: What was Gautam feeling after the call, and what shows it?
qa.a: Gautam felt invisible and doubtful, writing that there was nothing to mention and that maybe the others just think faster.

qa.q: What small change could Gautam try in tomorrow's internal review?
qa.a: Gautam could share the rural distribution point in the first few minutes, since it was already checked twice, instead of waiting for a perfect moment.

qa.q: How might Nikita see her own presentation, compared with how Gautam sees it?
qa.a: Nikita may have felt nervous or rushed inside, even though from outside Gautam only saw confidence.

grounding: It shows a new hire comparing inner doubt with a colleague's outer confidence and staying silent, then treating that invisibility as proof of adding little.
